subject.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout

question: Should Discord eventQueue.maxConcurrency bound unresolved listener promises even when timed-out listeners can occupy every slot indefinitely?
rationale: The code correctly enforces the documented concurrency bound, but it intentionally trades post-timeout continuation for bounded saturation when listeners cannot be cancelled; that availability policy requires maintainer ownership.

options.title: Bound actual listener work
options.body: Accept settlement-based slot release after live proof confirms timeout reporting, queued-event blocking, late settlement, and recovery behave operationally as intended.

options.title: Preserve timeout release
options.body: Keep releasing slots at listenerTimeout and accept that unresolved listener work may exceed maxConcurrency during timeout bursts.

options.title: Design cancellable listeners
options.body: Pause this patch and pursue an abortable listener contract, accepting substantially broader Carbon and plugin compatibility work.

recommendation.title: Bound actual listener work
recommendation.body: Accept settlement-based slot release after live proof confirms timeout reporting, queued-event blocking, late settlement, and recovery behave operationally as intended.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Discord runtime and dependency ownership makes them the strongest available candidate to judge Carbon listener cancellation limits and the channel availability tradeoff.
